https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadb.goal: Understand Network Load Balancer access logs (files, entries, processing) as an overview of the feature, which is enabled and disabled on separate pages

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/lates.goal: Grant AWS Config permission to deliver configuration history and snapshots to an existing Amazon S3 bucket by adding a bucket policy (including cross-account and IAM role / service-linked role considerations)

prerequisites.what: An existing Amazon S3 bucket to be used as the delivery channel destination (when not letting AWS Config create one automatically)
Access to the AWS Management Console in the account that owns the S3 bucket, with permission to edit the bucket policy
For cross-account delivery: IAM role assigned to the configuration recorder with explicit s3:ListBucket permission (for the HeadBucket call)

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrai.goal: Attach a bucket policy to an Amazon S3 bucket so that CloudTrail can write log files to it (including for organization trails)

prerequisites.what: An existing S3 bucket for CloudTrail log delivery. It must not be a Requester Pays bucket. The policy is attached to this bucket, so the reader may need to create it first.
A CloudTrail trail (its name and ARN) to reference in the bucket policy's aws:SourceArn condition, and a prefix if one is used

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/u.goal: Understand how to publish VPC flow log data to an Amazon S3 bucket (overview page that points to sub-pages for permissions and flow log creation)

prerequisites.what: An existing Amazon S3 bucket to receive the flow log files

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/lat.goal: Enable Amazon S3 server access logging on a source bucket so that access logs are delivered to a destination bucket in the same Region and account

prerequisites.what: Destination (target) S3 bucket in the same AWS Region and account as the source bucket, without Object Lock default retention, without Requester Pays, without server access logging enabled, and using SSE-S3 (not SSE-KMS) default encryption

Bucket policy on the destination bucket granting s3:PutObject to the logging service principal logging.s3.amazonaws.com (required when enabling programmatically via API/CLI/SDK; the console adds it automatically). Alternatively, ACL grants to the S3 log delivery group where ACLs are enabled.

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudF.goal: Enable CloudFront standard logging (legacy) for a distribution so that access logs are delivered to an Amazon S3 bucket

prerequisites.what: Amazon S3 bucket to receive the logs, in a default-enabled (not opt-in) region
ACLs enabled on the log bucket (S3 Object Ownership not set to bucket owner enforced)
Account permissions on the bucket (s3:GetBucketAcl, s3:PutBucketAcl) and an ACL granting the account FULL_CONTROL, so CloudFront can grant awslogsdelivery FULL_CONTROL
Key policy statement on the customer managed KMS key allowing CloudFront to write logs (plus kms:Decrypt if S3 Bucket Key is used), required only if the bucket uses SSE-KMS

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/lat.goal: Understand Amazon Redshift database audit logging (connection, user and user activity logs) and what is needed to export these logs to Amazon S3 or CloudWatch. The page is an overview; the enabling steps are on a separate page.

prerequisites.what: Amazon S3 bucket (existing or new) to receive audit logs, if logging to S3. It must use SSE-S3 (AES-256) encryption only and have S3 Object Lock turned off.
Bucket permissions that let the Amazon Redshift service call s3:GetBucketAcl and s3:PutObject on the log bucket
s3:PutObject permission on the log bucket for the user or IAM role that turns on logging
The enable_user_activity_logging database parameter set to true in the cluster parameter group (it is false by default). This is required for the user activity log.

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/lat.goal: Configure Amazon S3 Inventory so that scheduled lists of objects and metadata for a source bucket (or prefix) are published to a destination bucket, optionally encrypted with SSE-KMS

prerequisites.what: Destination S3 bucket that will receive the inventory report files (may be in another account)

Destination bucket policy granting Amazon S3 (service principal) permission to write inventory files to the destination bucket (created automatically only when using the console; manual for CLI/SDK/REST API and directory buckets, and the destination bucket owner must add it for cross-account)
AWS KMS customer managed key (not the aws/s3 managed key) for SSE-KMS encryption of inventory files, only if SSE-KMS is used
KMS key policy statement allowing Amazon S3 to use the customer managed key to encrypt inventory files (only for SSE-KMS)
IAM identity-based policy granting s3express:PutInventoryConfiguration and s3express:GetInventoryConfiguration (only for directory buckets)

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/lat.goal: Grant public read access to an S3 bucket configured as a static website by disabling Block Public Access settings and adding a bucket policy (plus object ACLs where needed)

prerequisites.what: An S3 bucket already configured as a static website (existing bucket to be made public)
Account-level Block Public Access settings must allow public access (edited/disabled if turned on), since the most restrictive of account and bucket settings applies

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ses/latest/d.goal: Grant Amazon SES the permissions it needs for email receiving actions (deliver to S3, use a KMS key, invoke Lambda, publish to an SNS topic in another account) by applying the example IAM, bucket, key, Lambda and SNS policies

prerequisites.what: S3 bucket that SES will write received email to
IAM role for the Deliver to S3 bucket action, which the permission policy and trust policy are attached to (required for buckets in regions without SES email receiving)
SES receipt rule and rule set containing the S3, Lambda, or SNS action (their names go into the policy conditions)
Customer managed AWS KMS key for encrypting received email (optional; the default aws/ses key needs no extra steps)
Amazon SNS topic for notifications (optional in the S3 role policy; in another account for the cross-account case)
AWS Lambda function for SES to invoke

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/lates.goal: Access, view and download Athena query results and query output files stored in an Amazon S3 query result location (or via managed query results)

IAM permissions for the principal: S3 GetObject on the query result location and Athena GetQueryResults action
Key permissions to encrypt and decrypt the query result location if it is encrypted (KMS key access)

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/lates.goal: Control and grant Athena users access to Amazon S3 buckets using identity-based policies, bucket resource policies, and access point policies

prerequisites.what: An Amazon S3 bucket (holding the data to be queried) that the policies apply to
An IAM user, group, or role to attach the identity-based policy to
S3 Access Grants configured to use trusted identity propagation identities (for Athena workgroups using IAM Identity Center authentication)

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/lat.goal: Configure IAM policies, roles and resource permissions so applications can send data to a Firehose stream and Firehose can ingest, process and deliver data to its sources and destinations (S3, S3 Tables, Iceberg, MSK, etc.)

CloudWatch log group and log stream for error logging
Private Amazon MSK cluster as the Firehose source, whose resource-based policy must be updated to allow the Firehose principal to call CreateVpcConnection

AWS Glue table definitions (and schema registry) for data format conversion
Amazon S3 table bucket and tables for the S3 Tables destination
AWS Lake Formation permissions granted to the Firehose delivery role (Lake Formation access control mode)

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/lat.goal: Set up the IAM permissions, the IAM role for Amazon S3 to assume, and (for cross-account setups) the destination bucket policy needed for S3 live replication

ACL grants from the owner of source-bucket objects owned by another AWS account, giving the role-owning account access to those objects (otherwise replication of them fails)

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-mana.goal: Enable or disable Session Manager session logging (to Amazon S3 and CloudWatch Logs) for managed nodes in an AWS account

The screen utility installed on Linux or macOS managed nodes so log data is not truncated

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/lat.goal: Generate a presigned URL to share a private Amazon S3 object with others for time-limited download, using the S3 console, AWS CLI, AWS SDKs (Python), AWS Toolkit for Visual Studio, or AWS Toolkit for VS Code

Connection from AWS Toolkit for Visual Studio to AWS (configured credentials)
AWS Toolkit for Visual Studio Code installed
Connection from AWS Toolkit for Visual Studio Code to AWS (configured credentials)

Destination Amazon S3 bucket to which data is written

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/lat.goal: Give an Amazon Redshift cluster permission to access other AWS resources (such as S3, DynamoDB, EMR) for COPY, UNLOAD, and CREATE LIBRARY by using role-based access control with an IAM role

IAM permissions policy on the role granting the minimum access for COPY, UNLOAD, and CREATE LIBRARY (e.g. LIST/GET/PUT on S3, SCAN/DESCRIBE on DynamoDB, ListInstances on EMR), such as AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess

AWS KMS key used to encrypt the S3 bucket contents
Customer-managed KMS key used to encrypt custom vocabularies, vocabulary filters, or custom language models

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudF.goal: Configure an Amazon S3 Object Lambda Access Point or S3 Access Point as the origin for a CloudFront distribution by adding the required resource permissions (Object Lambda Access Point policy, Access Point policy, bucket policy, Lambda permission)

AWSServiceRoleForOrganizations service-linked role in the management account (created automatically by Organizations)

Permissions for the creating user or role: AWSCloudTrail_FullAccess or equivalent, plus IAM and Organizations permissions to create the service-linked role and enable trusted access, and s3:PutEncryptionConfiguration if creating a new S3 bucket in the console

Destination general purpose bucket (in the same account) to receive replicated objects
Versioning enabled on the destination bucket (the console offers an Enable versioning button)

s3:GetObjectRetention and s3:GetObjectLegalHold permissions on the source bucket in the replication role (only if using Object Lock)
